function: Excluded (above_phy): the DRL learns the computation-offloading location (satellite or cloud) of IoT tasks, an edge-computing decision above the physical layer (pp. 1, 5, 8).
notes: Exclusion above_phy. The learned element is a DNN that outputs the binary offloading-location vector for 10 IoT devices (p. 5: "xn = 0 indicates that the task is computed locally on the satellite, and xn = 1 indicates that the task is computed at the cloud service center"; p. 8: "produces an output in the form of a floating-point N-dimensional vector"; Table III on p. 11 lists 10 output nodes). The abstract on p. 1 calls it a "deep reinforcement learning-based computation offloading decision algorithm". The only radio resource in the problem, the channel bandwidth, is not learned: p. 8: "DRLO employs channel bandwidth allocation algorithm based on the Lagrange multiplier method"; p. 10: "We employ a binary search method to solve for the Lagrange multiplier v". Although p. 7 writes the MDP action as (x_t, tau_t), the network output and the stored training labels are only the offloading vector (p. 8: "DRLO stores the inputs and decision as a triplet"), so no physical-layer decision is learned jointly with the offloading one. No physical-layer function (detection, channel estimation or feedback, precoding or beams, RIS, OTFS, ISAC, NTN power or beam control, over-the-air aggregation) is learned. Results (pp. 11-13) are a normalized cost ratio and run time, with a free-space path loss plus Rician fading channel (p. 11).
